thread:
jensen (acme): Hey team — we started getting reports from a bunch of Safari users that our live-transcript SSE stream sometimes delivers a few events then just stops delivering anything. The connection doesn't show an error, EventSource stays open but no more 'message' events. Happens only when customers are behind FastEdge CDN. Repro in-house only on Safari 16/17 so far.

amelia (support): Thanks Jensen — can you share a repro and some headers? Does the JS see 'onerror' triggers or just silence? Any console warnings?

jensen (acme): No onerror, just silence. The page shows streaming UI frozen but the socket is open. We tried a polyfill (eventsource-polyfill) — it reduces frequency of the hang but doesn't eliminate it. Console shows usual CORS preflight for another request but nothing obvious for the EventSource. Attaching a curl-ish repro from our edge:

```bash
# reproduce from our app host (force HTTP/1.1)
curl -v -N \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Origin: https://app.acme.com" \ 
  "https://live.acme.com/stream?session=abc123"
```

The response headers vary depending on cache: sometimes 200 with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Content-Encoding: gzip, sometimes 304 from the CDN (when we re-request) and then Safari stops.

maria (eng-runtime): Key suspects: CDN caching + gzip buffering + Safari's EventSource behavior. Known Safari quirk: if intermediate caches return 304s or if compression isn't flushed in streaming mode, events can be buffered until full gzip stream finishes, which makes it appear like the stream stopped. Also preflight + missing Vary headers can cause the edge to serve a cached 304 for a different auth state.

amelia (support): Can you paste an example of both 200 and 304 headers (copy raw) and the exact client-side EventSource instantiation?

jensen (acme): Sure — 200 case (works for a while):

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Connection: keep-alive
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Encoding: gzip
Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, stale-while-revalidate=60
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.acme.com

304 case (served by edge):

HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Connection: keep-alive
Cache-Control: public, max-age=0
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.acme.com

Client EventSource: new EventSource("/stream?session=abc123");

Note: we authenticate the user via a short-lived cookie set from the app domain; the CDN is configured to cache based on cookie currently (we tried both ways).

oliver (sre): A couple of immediate flags: 1) 304 responses for SSE are generally unsafe — SSE responses must be treated as non-cacheable and should never return 304 because partial I/O state is meaningless for a live stream. 2) gzip on chunked responses can be problematic at some proxies which buffer until gzip flush points. Safari is especially sensitive to buffering behavior.

maria (eng-runtime): Agreed. Repro steps we tried locally: we proxied the origin through a caching layer that returned 304 when If-Modified-Since matched; Safari client would open EventSource, receive 3 events, then edge returned 304 on a keepalive probe and Safari stopped delivering further events (no error). Nodejs origin was still streaming.

maria (eng-runtime): Suggested fixes to try quickly on origin/CDN: 
- Make SSE endpoint uncachable: `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform` and remove any ETag/Last-Modified to avoid conditional requests.
- Ensure CDN doesn't gzip or buffer streaming responses (turn off response compression for this path).
- Add explicit `Connection: keep-alive` and avoid Content-Length headers; use Transfer-Encoding: chunked from origin.
- Add `Vary: Authorization` or ensure the CDN forwards auth cookies instead of caching by cookie.

amelia (support): Also important for browsers: EventSource cannot set custom Authorization headers. If you're relying on an Authorization header from the app, browsers won't send that. Cookies are OK but the CDN must pass them/avoid caching. If you were trying to use a header via polyfill, that might explain why polyfill reduced but didn't remove the issue.

jensen (acme): We use cookie. We also tried a query-token approach (token in URL) but that was cached and exposed tokens in logs so we'd rather avoid it.

maria (eng-runtime): If you must keep CDN caching enabled for other endpoints, carve out the SSE path and set a rule: cache-bypass, strip ETag/Last-Modified, set `Cache-Control: no-store`, and disable compression at the edge. For CloudFront/Cloudflare, there's typically a way to create a route rule to 'pass through' for that path.

jensen (acme): Is there any QuickFix on the client side if we can't change CDN immediately?

oliver (sre): Client workarounds are limited. Options: 
- Use XHR/fetch streaming (fetch + ReadableStream) from JS where you control request headers (but CORS preflight will be involved and you need to handle reconnects manually).
- Long-poll fallback that reopens connections periodically.
- Keep the polyfill but ensure it disables using If-Modified-Since/ETag semantics.

maria (eng-runtime): We pushed a quick edge rule in the staging tenant to force no-store for /stream and disabled gzip for that path. deploy-bot: canary rollout to staging edge for rule "sse-no-cache-disable-compression" started.

deploy-bot: canary rollout successful to 12% edge nodes in staging (rule id sse-no-cache-disable-compression).

jensen (acme): After we pointed our test users at staging rules, Safari sessions maintained streaming for over 30 minutes with no stalls. Looks promising.

amelia (support): Great. Next steps: 1) schedule a targeted deploy in prod to set `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform` and remove ETag on sse path; 2) add CDN rule to disable gzip/buffering for this route; 3) monitor using a small Safari-only synthetic that reconnects and reports event gap counts.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll open an internal runtime ticket and include the nginx sample header config and Cloudflare worker snippet we used to repro:

```
# nginx origin snippet
location /stream {
  add_header Cache-Control "no-store, no-transform, private";
  add_header Vary "Authorization";
  gzip off;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive";
}
```

```js
// Cloudflare worker: pass-through for /stream
if (request.url.includes('/stream')) {
  const originResp = await fetch(request, { cf: { cacheEverything: false } });
  const headers = new Headers(originResp.headers);
  headers.set('Cache-Control', 'no-store, no-transform');
  headers.delete('ETag');
  headers.delete('Last-Modified');
  headers.set('Vary', 'Authorization');
  return new Response(originResp.body, { status: originResp.status, headers });
}
```

oliver (sre): Also add observability: count Safari sessions that see 0 events after initial N events and create an alert. That will catch regressions if a future change reintroduces 304s or compression.

jensen (acme): Thanks all — will try to prod prod edge change this week. Appreciate the quick triage. If we can't ship the CDN rule fast enough, we'll temporarily move to fetch-streaming on client as a fallback.

amelia (support): Closing the loop: we'll follow up when prod change is scheduled. Leaving thread open for any follow-up logs.
summary: Customer Safari SSE stalls due to CDN 304s and gzip buffering; workaround: make SSE uncachable, disable compression at edge, and ensure CDN passes auth/cookies. Repro snippets and nginx/worker config shared.
